rounds.reason: Initial complete proxy reconstruction of the continuous trench walk.
rounds.report:
Representation level: L1 (proxy). Three.js sampled-frame baseline (native inspect-revise protocol), not a Blender-equivalent reproduction.

Observed in the 24 reference samples (0-23.98 s, 2.39:1 letterboxed, one continuous take, no cuts):
- 0-6 s: a camera leading two helmeted WWI soldiers backwards through a narrow, dark timber-lined trench. The round-faced lead soldier ("Blake") is close to camera, his companion ("Schofield") behind him and image-right.
- 6-9 s: the camera swings round the pair's right side (motion-blurred pan at 6.3 s, side view of the pair facing each other at 7.3 s, profile of Schofield at 8.3 s).
- 9-24 s: the camera follows behind the soldiers down an open, sandbagged trench under an overcast sky, with spoil heaps, telegraph poles, dugouts and seated/standing/crouching soldiers on the right. A sergeant approaches facing them (9.4 s), turns and leads; Schofield drops back out of frame on the left (~11.5 s); the camera stays just behind Blake; the sergeant turns back to talk to him (19.8-20.9 s) and walks on.

Reconstruction:
- Geometry: boxes/cylinders/spheres. Soldiers are articulated proxies (pelvis, torso, hips/knees, shoulders/elbows, neck/head with helmet dome+brim, webbing plate, pack, slung rifle on the observed shoulder). Trench: mud floor, earth walls, sandbag rows, half-buried cylinder spoil heaps, revetment posts, tall dark timber section for the opening, dugout openings with benches, fire step, telegraph poles with wires, distant closing mounds. 12 static extras (sitting/standing/crouching) plus two walkers further ahead.
- Articulation: analytic walk cycle (hip/knee/arm swing, bob) whose amplitude follows each walker's world speed; head and body turns keyed for the 7.3 s exchange, Blake's 10.4 s glance at Schofield, and the sergeant's turn-around at ~10 s and turn-back to talk at ~20 s.
- Camera: one continuous camera keyed relative to Blake from per-sample estimates of subject image position and helmet size (vertical FOV 48 deg for the 16:9 frame; black letterbox bars attached to the camera); Hermite interpolation between samples; small deterministic handheld shake/bob. Light intensity lowered for the timber section (about 2.5-6 s).
- Timing: absolute-time update, 576 frames at 23.976 fps; Blake walks at a constant 0.9 m/s.

Inference vs. observation: subject placements at the 24 sample times are estimated from the images; the camera swing path between 6.3 and 9.4 s, Schofield's whereabouts after ~12 s, walking speed, and extras' exact positions are inferred.

Render feedback: none received yet (initial generation).

- Appearance is deliberately proxy-level: flat earth/sandbag/timber surfaces with no sandbag texture, cables or corrugation; soldiers are box/sphere proxies without faces (hair cap only marks the back of the head).
- The lead-in timber trench is brighter and more uniform than the very dark reference; the open trench is still somewhat warmer than the grey-green reference grade.
- The 6-9 s camera swing is an inferred path between three samples; Schofield's exact body/head orientation at 7.3 and 8.3 s and his position after he leaves frame (~11.5 s) are inferred.
